Appreciate the draft SOW and the options. A few quick clarifying questions from our side before procurement will engage:

- How long is the price hold for the on-demand shelter you have in the spreadsheet? Procurement wants a minimum 90-day guarantee, but we may prefer 180 days if possible.
- Does the carry-forward credit apply to committed uplift only or to baseline too?

Sarah / Naomi —

Thanks — quick note from pricing/legal perspective. We can offer two pragmatic constructs which tend to satisfy procurement and preserve predictable economics for both parties:

Option A (shelter):
- Price hold for bursts above committed baseline for 180 days from contract effective date.
- Shelter applies to up to 3x the committed monthly baseline, after which on-demand incremental charges apply at +15% to standard hosted rate (this preserves burst-headroom economics).
- Unused committed uplift credits: carry-forward up to one quarter and can be used to offset overage invoices in the following quarter.

Option B (tiered credit):
- No shelter. Instead, a tiered credit schedule: 5% credit for usage between 100–150% of committed, 10% credit for 150–250%, and 20% credit for sustained >250% (sustained = 2 consecutive months).
- Credits apply as billing offsets only (not a cash refund).

On model family: pricing in the workbook is separated by model family and quantization profile. If you shift traffic to a quantized variant, we can reflect that in the usage ledger and your effective unit cost will reduce as shown in column D of the workbook.

Kimberly — can legal confirm this shelter wording is standard-friendly? We will prepare a short amendment to the existing MSA to capture the shelter mechanics and the carry-forward credit.

I can also produce the break-even scenarios Naomi mentioned (two-case comparison) by EOD.

Cheers,
Marcus

Sarah —

Thanks for the questions and for sending the PO template. Summarizing a recommended path that (a) meets procurement's preference for a minimum guarantee, (b) protects you during the early rollout, and (c) keeps the commercial simple:

Recommended (combines Option A + limited tier):
- 12-month renewal, committed uplift = +20% baseline (applies to license + inference unit commitments).
- On-demand rate shelter: 180-day price hold on burst usage up to 3x committed baseline. After that, incremental usage billed at +10% over standard hosted rate (we reduced from Marcus's +15% as a one-time concession for ScaleRetail).
- Carry-forward: unused committed uplift credits carry forward one quarter and can offset overage invoices in the next quarter.
- Billing: net-45 per ScaleRetail template, amendment to MSA to capture shelter mechanics.

Next steps:
1) Naomi to upload the amendment + final SOW into the HubSpot deal record (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/6789) by EOD Monday.

3) Legal (Kimberly) to draft the short amendment and send for redline; target final execution by 3/15.

If that aligns, Marcus and I will update the pricing workbook to reflect the reduced incremental surcharge and prepare a 2-case break-even comparison (baseline vs. 2x uplift) for your CFO.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we want to make this as operationally frictionless as possible for your rollout.

Warmly,
